## Overview
### Introduction to Google: Nano Banana 2
The Google: Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview) model, released by Google on 2024-01-01, is a standard-tier, non-open-source language model. This model is part of the Gemini series and is designed to provide a balance between performance and cost. With its architecture, it supports various capabilities such as text, function calling, JSON mode, streaming, and structured outputs, making it a versatile tool for developers.

### Technical Strengths and Use-Cases
The Google: Nano Banana 2 model boasts a context window of 65,536 tokens and a maximum output of 65,536 tokens, allowing it to handle complex and lengthy inputs. Its knowledge cutoff is 2023-12, ensuring it has a broad and up-to-date understanding of the world. The model excels in chat, text generation, coding, analysis, RAG pipelines, and summarization tasks, thanks to its high MMLU benchmark score of 80.0 and an LMSYS Arena ELO score of 1200. However, its pricing structure, with input costing $0.5 per 1M tokens and output costing $3.0 per 1M tokens, should be carefully considered when planning applications.

### Pricing and Cost Considerations
When using the Google: Nano Banana 2 model, developers should be aware of the pricing structure to optimize their costs. For example, 1,000 calls with an average of 500 tokens would cost approximately $0.0018, while 100,000 calls would amount to $0.18. Given its capabilities and strengths, this model is best suited for applications that require advanced text processing and generation. Despite not having direct competitors listed, the model's unique combination of features and pricing makes it an attractive option for developers looking to integrate AI into their projects, especially those focused on chat, coding, and analysis tasks.
